newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo clarifies privatisation of plantations.
newsitem.headline: Colombo clarifies privatisation of plantations.

text.p: Sri Lanka, naming six plantation firms for sale by tender, on Tuesday said only pre-qualified concerns could bid for a controlling stake in them.
The Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC) said those willing to bid would have to express interest first and be pre-qualified to ensure a more level playing field.
"Bidders who show adequate financial resources and have a good track record in the sector, will be invited to take part in a competitive bidding process," a PERC official told Reuters.

Under the new conditions, the commission has called for expressions of interest for the sale of 51 percent in the plantation firms of Maturata, Elkaduwa, Elpitiya, Namunukula, Kahawatte and Malwatta Valley. The closing date for expressions of interest is October 25.
"We have changd to a customary bidding process by pre-qualified parties from selling controlling stakes on the stock exchange," the PERC official said.
The government began privatising the 23 estate firms late last year by selling 51 percent of those firms on an all-or-none basis on the stock exchange.
Controlling interest in 13 firms have been sold so far with six already traded on the Colombo bourse.

"Some of the unsuccessful bidders alleged that the funds used to buy 51 percent stakes could have come from dubious sources, and that some buyers did not have the expertise to manage the firms," the official said.
The government hopes to complete privatisation of the plantation sector by the end of 1996.
